title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the Committee’s 2020 report on AI and public standards, outlining its commitments to make artificial intelligence safer and more transparent for the public. It stresses that AI must be developed and used responsibly, with clear rules and oversight to protect people’s privacy, safety, and democratic values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector to keep tests fair and trustworthy. The policy aims to set clear rules and safeguards, ensuring that AI tools are used responsibly, transparently, and in a way that supports quality and equality in education.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report evaluates how copyright‑protected materials are used to train and develop AI systems, examining the legal and ethical implications of this practice. It offers an impact assessment and provides recommendations to balance innovation with protecting creators’ rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government outlines its plan to address the House of Lords Select Committee’s concerns about AI, emphasizing strong regulation and investment in safe AI development. It commits to supporting research, ensuring ethical standards, and protecting jobs while preventing misuse of AI technologies.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document explains the terms of reference for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence relates to public standards, including FAQs to clarify key points. It sets out the committee’s objectives, scope, responsibilities, and guidelines for its work on AI and public standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence. Their submission aims to inform the committee on key AI governance matters.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explores how the use of artificial intelligence will change the rules that govern medical products, focusing on safety, efficacy, and transparency. It outlines how to apply the principles from the AI White Paper so that developers, regulators, and patients can trust AI-driven medical technologies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This strategy outlines how the Defence organisation will develop and use artificial intelligence to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence organisation in the world relative to its size. It focuses on building capabilities, fostering innovation, and ensuring ethical and responsible use of AI across all defence operations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan shows how the Department for Transport will team up with the transport industry to unlock AI’s benefits and tackle its challenges. It seeks to boost safer, more efficient travel while carefully managing the risks that new AI technologies bring.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This document gives an update on how copyrighted works are being used to train and develop AI systems. It reviews progress under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, noting achievements, challenges, and policy suggestions.
